title: Progressive tool-result injection for streaming responses with recursion sentinel
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem / Motivation:
Redwood's core API supports streaming generation and function/tool calling, but a gap remains when multiple tools are chained within a single streaming session: tool outputs must be injected back into the live stream in a way that preserves structured output contracts, remains backward-compatible with older SDKs, and prevents unbounded recursion or loop amplification when a model calls tools that in turn trigger further tool calls. This ticket designs and implements a progressive injection mechanism plus a lightweight recursion sentinel to keep client streams predictable and safe.

Goals:
1) Allow tool results to be injected progressively into an active streaming response (partial fields and full payloads) without breaking structured-output schemas clients expect.
2) Provide a compatibility shim so older SDKs that expect JSON-at-end receive a compatible envelope.
3) Enforce recursion/loop guards with circuit-breaker semantics and clear diagnostics when a tool-call chain exceeds configured bounds.
4) Instrument telemetry for routing/latency/cost impact and expose per-request annotations in Console.

Design summary:
- Streaming envelope: introduce a minimal framing protocol over existing SSE/websocket streams with three event types: stream_chunk, tool_inject, stream_meta. Each event contains an event-type string and a base64-encoded payload when binary-safe is needed. The envelope is opt-in via a new Accept header `Accept: application/redwood-stream+json;version=1` so we remain compatible with existing clients.
- Progressive injection: when an orchestrator invokes a tool during generation, tool results are sent back as one or more tool_inject events. We provide a deterministic insertion cursor (e.g., inject_after_token_id or inject_at_boundary) so downstream consumers can render partial structured fields as they arrive.
- Structured output validation: injected payloads must include a small provenance header (tool_key, call_id, schema_hash). We validate schema_hash against the serving model's declared structured output schema and reject injections that would violate the final contract.
- Recursion sentinel: add a per-request counter (tool_depth) and cumulative token budget (tool_token_budget). Both are passed through the KV/session metadata and enforced by the orchestrator. If tool_depth > configured_limit or token budget exhausted, orchestrator emits a stream_meta event with a machine-readable error code (TOOL_RECURSION_LIMIT) and automatically falls back to a graceful summary injection or a deterministic no-op tool result depending on policy.
- Compatibility shim: for SDKs that do not opt into the new envelope, we also provide a compatibility mode on the server that collates tool_inject events into a final JSON field `injected_tool_results` and appends it just before the final model end-of-stream chunk. This keeps older integrations working with a small latency tradeoff.

Implementation plan / Tasks:
- Runtime: add stream envelope encoder/decoder in the serving runtime and HTTP gateway. (ENG)
- Orchestrator: propagate tool_depth and tool_token_budget in request contexts; add enforcement hooks. (ENG)
- SDKs: expose new streaming client option and backwards-compatible decoder for older clients. (devexp)
- Console: surface stream_meta events and recursion incidents in per-request traces and the Rollouts dashboard. (product/console)
- E2E tests: create scenarios that chain 2-6 tools and assert correct injection ordering, schema validation, and sentinel activation. (qa)

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for stream envelope encode/decode and tool_inject ordering.
- Orchestrator enforces configured tool_depth <= default(3) and token budget defaults to 2048 tokens; both values configurable per-customer.
- SDK compatibility shim returns an identical end-state JSON for clients that do not opt into streaming envelope.
- Console shows per-request stream_meta events and a sampled telemetry dashboard for injection frequency and average latency.
- No customer-facing regressions for existing non-streaming integrations.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Extra CPU for envelope encoding/decoding at high QPS. Mitigation: fast-path binary framing and re-use buffers; add perf budget to runtime-1.19.
- Risk: Tool calls create amplification loops. Mitigation: strict defaults (tool_depth=3) and hard token budgets; provide admin overrides via Dedicated/Private configs.
- Risk: Schema mismatches cause partial renders. Mitigation: schema_hash validation and optional strict vs. permissive injection modes; permissive mode logs warnings but still injects sanitized payloads.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged opt-in on hosted for a small percentage of traffic with telemetry sampling.
2) Roll SDK updates alongside the server so devexp customers can test streaming envelope behavior.
3) Enable compatibility shim for remaining traffic with a 48h monitoring window.
4) Expose admin knobs in Console for token budgets and depth limits.

Notes / References:
- Prototype design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Progressive+Streaming+Tool+Injection
- Example PR (runtime encoder): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1487
- UX mockups for Console trace: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleTraceMockups

2026-02-16 - Diego Martinez: Proposed framing protocol in design doc, added Accept header opt-in to avoid breaking existing clients.
2026-02-18 - Mina Johnson (Product): Please add a Console visualization for stream_meta errors; added to Console backlog.

2026-02-20 - Diego Martinez: Implemented runtime encoder prototype; opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1487. Benchmarks show +3% CPU at 1000rps, will optimize buffers next sprint.
2026-02-23 - Security review kickoff: flagged compatibility shim as needing review for potential information exposure; security review assigned to Rajiv Kapoor.
2026-02-26 - QA: Added E2E tests for tool_depth exhaustion; tests simulate 5 chained tools and assert TOOL_RECURSION_LIMIT emitted as stream_meta.
2026-02-28 - Diego Martinez: Merged runtime prototype after buffer optimizations; next steps SDK changes and Console trace plumbing.
testing_plan: Unit tests for envelope encode/decode, integration tests for multi-tool chains (2..6 tools), stress test to measure CPU/latency impact at target QPS, backward-compatibility smoke tests with older SDKs. Add sampling to production for first 48h to capture stream_meta events.
implementation_notes: Use lightweight base64 payloads only when necessary; prefer compact JSON fragments for textual injections. Store provenance header (tool_key, call_id, schema_hash) as a 3-field CSV in the stream header to minimize parse cost.
acceptance_definition: All CI tests pass, compatibility shim verified against v1 SDKs, Console shows stream_meta events for sampled requests, defaults enforce depth=3 and token budget=2048, and security signoff obtained.
